title: The Key To Motivating Students
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that genuine student motivation requires an ingredient many teachers avoid discussing: a willingness to let students fail. Once students trust that a teacher genuinely cares about them, the teacher's words of encouragement carry real weight — but that trust must be paired with real stakes, meaning the teacher won't reteach endlessly, coddle through assignments, or accept inadequate work just to pass a student. He criticizes a broader educational culture, encouraged by administrators and professional development, that treats doing more and more for students as a virtue, arguing it instead breeds helplessness, boredom, and burnout for both students and teachers. When real failure is possible, he contends, students feel purposeful responsibility that activates genuine motivation and grit, born from a total shift of responsibility from teacher to student.
points: Genuine motivation requires students to know the teacher genuinely cares about them, which makes encouragement carry real weight.
The key, counterintuitive ingredient is a willingness to let students actually fail rather than endlessly coddle or reteach.
Linsin criticizes the broader educational culture that treats "doing more" for students as virtuous, arguing it instead breeds helplessness and burnout.
Real motivation is described as born of vibrant lessons, clear instruction, and a total shift of responsibility from teacher to student.
quotes: Just knowing that you have their best interest at heart causes students to trust you and believe in what you say.
Coming from someone they trust and admire, the right words spoken at the right time can light a fire under even the most apathetic students .
It is this: You have to be willing to let your students fail .
In educational circles, there is a reluctance to allow students to learn hard lessons. It’s become a badge of honor—as well as an expectation—for teachers to do more and be more for their students.
The only thing students learn from a teacher who won’t let them fail is helplessness. They only thing they learn is that they can’t .
They develop grit and the mindset that they can get better at anything through hard work .
It’s borne of a teacher who communicates unconditional love for their students.
